newsitem.title: POLAND: CZECH REP, POLAND LEAD E.EUROPE INVESTMENT POLL.
newsitem.headline: CZECH REP, POLAND LEAD E.EUROPE INVESTMENT POLL.

text.p: Investment risk in 14 east and
central European countries is smallest in the Czech Republic,
with Poland second and Hungary third, a survey conducted every
six months by an independent Polish research institute said.
The Gdansk-based Research Institute for Market Economy
(IBnGR) for the first time did not include in its survey East
Germany, which six months ago led the ranking followed by the
Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland.
"The Czech Republic is becoming the region's leader as the
investment risk there is clearly falling down, but the distance
between Poland and Czech Republic is narrowing," an anlyst at
the IBnGR Zbigniew Dworzecki told a news conference.
He stressed that the whole Eastern and Central European
region was becoming safer and more attractive for foreign
investment as its countries had improved their legal systems
and economic situation.
He said Poland was the most attractive country in the
region and pointed out it was likely to keep its high position,
mostly due to its planned privatisations.
"Poland has got very good development perspectives as
investors are interested in large markets and large potentials
- there is growing interest in Poland and its purchasing
power," he said.
"The Polish privatisation programme is likely to attract
large capital, which is waiting for openings in certain sectors
such as telecommunications and transport," he added.
He said Russia, Czech Republic, Hungary followed Poland in
the ranking.
THE RISK OF INVESTMENT MEASURED IN A SCALE FROM ONE TO FIVE
WITH FIVE BEING THE HIGHEST RISK:
Czech Republic 2.0 (2.1)
Poland 2.4 (2.5)
Hungary 2.6 (2.4)
Slovenia 2.8 (2.9)
Slovakia 3.0 (3.1)
Estonia 3.0 (3.3)
NOTE. Comparative data from the previous poll six months ago
in brackets.
